dependencies: native full-root phase and ring pairing
mechanism_tested: Measure the deep normal subgroup pi^c A before attempting a reduced-class receiver; compare coherent character retention and public Fourier/feedforward pointer erasure.
local_result: Measured outputs identify s and s+pi^(c+1)A for every fixed native label cohort and arbitrary batch size; coherent outputs need not.
positive_control: Public conjugate-basis pointer measurement and known normal-action correction restore the original input including entanglement, but do not decode or erase its word index.
cut: Do not promote irreversible deep normal-character measurement to free growing-depth central descent.
proof_obligations: External review of the annihilator-ideal calculation and actual integer-secret precision bound.
A constructive decoder must act jointly on words and characters or otherwise preserve cross-character phases.
Charge clean word/fiber erasure, inter-sector mixing and source error; coherent public hash computation alone supplies none.
Keep additional untouched originals and preceding arbitrary noncommuting operations outside the exact-channel bound.
Check prior literature before any novelty claim.
falsifiers: A phase difference is not constant in a claimed character class.
The normal-dual quotient is computed at the wrong pi-adic root.
Raw character outcomes are dropped or reweighted by the secret.
The class2 group-projection ceiling of one integer trit is incorrectly substituted for this channel's two-trit ceiling.
The measured-channel bound is promoted to a coherent or arbitrary-receiver lower bound.
Conjugate pointer erasure is said to undo already classically measured characters or to decode the secret.
